page.title: Virtual event production services explained
page.description: Learn what virtual event production covers, from platform choice to live crew, rehearsals, backup streams, and post‑event delivery.
page.h1: What is included in virtual event production services?
page.definition: Virtual event production services are the end‑to‑end crew, run‑of‑show, rehearsal, backup stream, branding assets, live moderation and edited recording that turn a platform into a polished online experience delivered on the platform you already use such as Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24 or StreamYard.
page.quick_answer: Book a full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before the event and confirm a backup stream is ready. West Peek Productions produces virtual, hybrid and webinar events and sets up marketing, content and creative operations.

sections.h2: What deliverables should a production contract specify?

blocks.p: A production contract should list every asset the crew will hand over so you can approve them before the live day.

ul: branded slide template and lower thirds

sections.h2: How long does a typical virtual event production take?

blocks.p: A webinar needs three to four weeks from brief to live while a summit or online conference needs six to eight weeks.

sections.h2: Which roles are needed for a webinar versus a summit?

blocks.p: A simple webinar can run with one producer but a summit or hybrid event requires a show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator.

sections.h2: What platform and production costs should I expect?

blocks.p: Platform fees follow three cost models while production fees range from $2,500 to $7,500 for a moderated webinar and $10,000 to $50,000 and above for executive summits.

ul: per‑host licences sized by attendee capacity (Zoom Webinars)
annual contracts quoted by sales (ON24, Cvent, Bizzabo, Goldcast)

sections.h2: How do I manage post‑event follow‑up and reporting?

blocks.p: Send the replay within 24 to 48 hours while attendees still remember the event and feed engagement data into your CRM for nurture campaigns.

faq.q: When should I schedule the full rehearsal?
faq.a: Run the full rehearsal on the actual platform two to five days before the event, then do a technical check sixty minutes before going live to catch any last‑minute issues. This ensures speaker audio, video, slides and backup stream all work together.

faq.q: What is the difference between platform and production?
faq.a: The platform is the software that hosts the stream while production is the crew, cameras, encoder, run of show and backup stream that make the broadcast professional. You purchase both separately and the production team works on the platform you choose.

faq.q: How many people are needed to run a hybrid conference?
faq.a: A hybrid conference typically needs a show caller, speaker manager, moderator, platform operator and on‑site AV liaison, plus a backup producer for redundancy. Each role owns a specific workstream so nothing falls through the cracks. This staffing model matches the eight workstreams defined for large events.

faq.q: What should I include in the post‑event report?
faq.a: Include attendance numbers, average watch time, poll and chat engagement, lead scores from CRM sync, and a summary of edited clips distributed across channels. Add qualitative feedback from speaker debriefs and note any technical incidents for future improvement. This gives stakeholders a clear view of ROI and informs the next event plan.
